section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how Torah and prayer correspond to the higher and lower levels of Daas, and how Yehudah's approach unites them.
section.t: And 4)
Based on this, we can explain the connection of "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" to the union of the two intellects,
the higher Daas and the lower Daas,
for the two matters of Torah and prayer are in the manner of higher Daas and lower Daas.
For in addition to the fact that Torah is from above downward and prayer is from below upward
(for higher Daas is from above downward and lower Daas is from below upward53),
[there is also the fact] that Torah is drawn into the intellect of man as it is in his [own] existence
(for although man's intellect is incomparable to the Torah,
nevertheless, in order for man's intellect to understand and grasp the Torah he learns, he does not need to depart from his [own] existence)
and even then it is the word of Hashem54,
meaning that the drawing down of Torah below is not according to the limitations of the lower realm, but rather from the aspect of the Torah itself
(since it is without limit, it is drawn into every place),
this indicates that in the drawing down of Torah, the creations do not occupy a place — this is higher Daas, where
(above there is a "yesh" [existence], and)
below there is nothing.
And [the fact] that the drawing down of prayer is from the aspect of the elevation of the lower realm's service
("You desire the work of Your hands"),
and also that its subject is to change the creations,
indicates that in this drawing down, the lower realm occupies a place — this is lower Daas, where below there is a "yesh."
And through Yehudah's plea "Bi Adoni,"
which is like the matter of the verse "Ad-nai, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise" recited before prayer
(as above in section 3),
his prayer
(the prayer of man)
was in such a manner that through it, the prayer of the Holy One, blessed be He, was drawn down,
[so that] even the drawing down through his prayer,
whose subject is to make a change in the lower realm,
was in a manner that the drawing down from above was revealed within it
(from above the chain of descent),
[this is] the union of the two intellects.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that when prayer incorporates the advantage of Torah, it surpasses Torah, just as lower Daas illuminated by higher Daas surpasses higher Daas.
section.t: And based on what was explained above
(section 4)
that prayer is above Torah
[for Torah is analogous to the matter of "lower and lower," etc., and prayer is analogous to the matter of "higher and higher," etc.],
and the advantage of Torah relative to prayer is that the drawing down of Torah is a drawing down of Elokus,
it can be said
that when prayer is in a manner that also contains the advantage of Torah,
then prayer is above Torah.
And similarly, regarding higher Daas and lower Daas,
when lower Daas is in a manner that the revelation of higher Daas also shines within it,
then it is above higher Daas.
And similarly, regarding Zeir Anpin and Malchus,
which are higher Daas and lower Daas
(as above in section 2),
[it is] that through Malchus becoming like Zeir Anpin
(both equal),
this is a preparation for the revelation of the source of Malchus, which is above the source of Zeir Anpin.
Therefore, in the union of the two intellects in "Vayigash eilav Yehudah," there is also concealed the elevation of Malchus that will be in the future,
that Malchus will be above Zeir Anpin,
"A woman of valor is the crown of her husband."
